task:
Perform a read-only current-main acceptance and replacement audit of open PR #526, `Harden PostgreSQL 18 production-candidate promotion tooling`, head `2e79945d28ba3922573dd100598223037fa51b9f`, against current origin/main `fd64ef8e14b5b026cec2d14949115ab681fb0b7d`. Read CLAUDE.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, the complete PR diff and all paginated top-level comments, formal reviews, inline review comments and unresolved review threads, plus all current-main files touched by the PR and relevant tests/runbooks. Do not modify files, commit, push, merge, deploy, access any remote host or production system, use secrets, connect to any database, run migrations/backfills, change DNS, start/stop containers, or make any external state change.

The audit must determine whether #526 should be repaired on a current-main replacement branch, split into smaller changes, or closed as superseded. Verify every review finding directly against the exact head and current main. Build a deduplicated findings ledger containing: severity, exact path/behavior, whether still applicable, concrete evidence, required repair, and whether the thread is outdated only because code moved versus actually resolved. Include at minimum the known areas: exported DSNs being overwritten by `.env`; DSNs in process argv; trusted immutable audit revision; server/database identity; role separation and migration ownership; least-privilege compatibility; repeatable-read snapshot; stale topology/regional/cluster/economy coverage; intentionally unresolved station associations; read-replica writer endpoints; audit runtime bounds at production scale; direct-runbook reviewed revision; and any newer current-main incompatibility.

Compare the PR's migration/deploy/operator contracts with current main and identify overlap with #527, #537, and any merged later work. Do not assume all old findings are correct: verify them. Determine a safe dependency order and propose the smallest coherent replacement slices, each with exact files and focused tests. Explicitly distinguish repository code repair from owner-only operational evidence or production actions. End with: recommendation (repair/split/close), complete findings ledger, exact proposed slices and order, tests each slice would need, and hard blockers. No implementation in this run.
